title: Booleans & Type Conversion
objective: Use true/false values and recognize which values JavaScript treats as truthy or falsy.

sourceAlignment.title: JavaScript Crash Course
sourceAlignment.author: Nick Morgan
sourceAlignment.note: Alignment metadata only. Lesson prose and exercises are original Code Forge material.

paragraphs: A boolean is either true or false — there are only ever these two values, and comparisons produce one of them. You write them without quotes; they're not strings.

JavaScript will treat almost any value as a boolean when it needs to, in a condition, using a rule called truthy/falsy. Exactly six values count as falsy: 0, "" (empty string), null, undefined, NaN, and false itself. Every other value — including "0" as a string, or an empty array — counts as truthy.

Boolean(value), String(value), and Number(value) explicitly convert a value to that type on demand, rather than relying on JavaScript to guess. Boolean(0) is false, Boolean("") is false, Boolean("hello") is true.
explanation.rule: Only 0, "", null, undefined, NaN, and false are falsy — everything else, including "0" and empty arrays, is truthy.

examples.title: Falsy Values
examples.note: The number 0 and the empty string are falsy, but the string "0" (a non-empty string) is truthy, along with any other non-empty string.

checks.question: What does Boolean("0") evaluate to?
options: true, because "0" is a non-empty string.

feedback.correct: Correct — "0" is a non-empty string, so it's truthy even though it looks like the number zero.
feedback.incorrect: Only the number 0 and the empty string "" are falsy — the string "0" has a character in it, so it's truthy.

assignment.title: Truthy Check
assignment.brief: Write describeValue(value) that logs true if Boolean(value) is true, and false otherwise.
assignment.outputCheckLabel: describeValue(0) then describeValue('hello') log false then true

hints: Boolean(value) converts value to true or false directly.
0 is falsy, so describeValue(0) should log false.
"hello" is a non-empty string, so it's truthy.
Log the result of Boolean(value), not value itself.
